Six Palestinians have been killed and 38 others wounded in Israeli attacks across Gaza in the last 24 hours, the enclave's health ministry reports.

This brings the overall toll of Palestinians killed in Gaza by Israel since the so-called ceasefire was imposed in October last year to 1,574, wth 5,867 wounded.

articles.summary: Israeli security forces arrested at least 13 Palestinians on Thursday in raids across the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian sources. Those arrested included three brothers, the Prisoners’ Media Office and local sources said. Paramedic and anti-settlement activist Bashar al-Qaryouti was also arrested, the sources reported. In Hebron, Israeli forces continued raids and closures for the seventh consecutive day, shutting iron gates around the Old City and seizing Palestinian homes in the Jalda and Ain Deir Baha neighborhoods for use as military barracks, local sources told Anadolu. The Hebron Municipality said Tuesday that the raids had displaced nearly 5,000 Palestinians, making up 780 families. articles.summary:
West Bank: 14 Palestinians arrested, two wounded by settler attacks and homes demolished

Israeli troops have detained 14 Palestinians across Nablus, Jenin and Bethlehem as military raids and settler attacks continue across the occupied West Bank.

According to Wafa news agency, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians attempting to gather olives in Kafr Malik, northeast of Ramallah, while two Palestinians were wounded and seven others arrested by Israeli forces during a military siege of Hebron.

Menawhile, in Jerusalem, Israeli forces razed a two-storey home without a permit, and three other houses were demolished across three towns in the Salfit governorate.

Wafa further reported that 66 Hebron schools have been shuttered, leaving 2,872 students without tuition.

articles.title: Smotrich calls on Shin Bet to question Palestinian party leaders over foreign interference claims
articles.summary:
Smotrich calls on Shin Bet to question Palestinian party leaders over foreign interference claims

Israel's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called on Shin Bet to question Palestinian party leaders over claims of foreign influence in the election, Israeli news site Haaretz reports.

According to the report, Smotrich said, "Suspicions of election manipulation using foreign Islamist money are a test for the State of Israel" and that "Arab party leaders must be questioned by the Shin Bet today".

His comments come after the Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg called for an investigation into suspected foreign influence on the elections.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud Party responded that "Israel's election was stolen!"

"This is an attack on democracy aimed at enabling a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel and the toppling of right-wing rule in order to force an Israeli withdrawal and defeat for the IDF on all fronts, foremost among them Iran," it said.

Meanwhile, Democrats leader Yair Golan said in a post on X that Netanyahu is trying "to undermine the election results through an ugly campaign to delegitimize the public's will, and the Arab public in particular".

With more than 90 percent of votes counted, preliminary election results point to a deadlock between Netanyahu’s outgoing bloc and the Zionist opposition.

Neither side has secured the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority, partly due to Palestinian-led parties winning a projected record 19 seats.

Palestinian-led parties have offered to support an opposition-led minority government to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power. But key opposition figures have rejected the prospect of governing with Arab parties.

articles.title: Over 29,000 double-envelope ballots counted in Israeli election, around 6% of total
articles.summary: More than 29,000 double-envelope ballots, around 6% of the total, have been counted in Israel’s elections, with the Central Elections Committee expecting the count to conclude by the afternoon, Israeli media reported Thursday. A total of 29,253 double-envelope ballots have been counted out of nearly 500,000, the daily Yedioth Ahronoth noted. Double-envelope ballots are used by voters casting their votes away from their registered polling stations, including soldiers, diplomats, police officers, and displaced residents. Officials check identification details on the outer envelope to prevent duplicate voting, then separate it from the anonymous ballot before counting. The remaining votes could change individual parties’ seat totals and the balance between the rival blocs. READ: Israel’s final election results expected Thursday evening: Election official […]

Iran’s army says it downed MQ-1 drone east of Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) intercepted and destroyed an MQ-1 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz, the semi-official ISNA news agency reported Thursday, citing the force. The IRGC said the drone was the 14th MQ-1 to be intercepted and destroyed by its air defense system. According to ISNA, the incident took place in the skies east of the Strait of Hormuz, opposite the coastal area of Sirik. The MQ-1 drone is a US-made unmanned aerial vehicle, although the IRGC did not specify the drone’s operator in its statement. The incident comes amid growing signs of a possible new round of US and Israeli offensive action against Iran. archive.security_status_cs: Izrael čelí patové situaci po parlamentních volbách, kde ani jeden blok nezískal jasnou většinu, což komplikuje politickou stabilitu. Na íránské frontě mezitím dochází k eskalaci po sestřelení amerického dronu íránskými revolučními gardami v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu, ač probíhají diplomatické snahy o příměří. Humanitární krize v Gaze nadále zůstává vážným bezpečnostním a politickým problémem.
archive.security_status_en: Israel faces a political deadlock after elections where neither major bloc secured a clear majority, complicating internal stability. Meanwhile, tensions with Iran have escalated following the IRGC's downing of a US drone near the Strait of Hormuz, even as diplomatic efforts for a ceasefire are underway. The humanitarian crisis in Gaza also remains a severe security and political pressure point.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekávají intenzivní vyjednávání o možných povolebních koalicích v Izraeli a sledování reakcí Washingtonu na íránské incidenty v Hormuzském průlivu. Bezpečnostní složky zůstanou ve vysoké pohotovosti.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will feature intense negotiations regarding post-election coalitions in Israel and close monitoring of Washington's response to Iranian incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. Security forces will remain on high alert.

archive.security_status_cs: Izrael čelí hluboké politické krizi a patové situaci po volbách, kde Netanjahuův blok nezískal většinu a objevují se obvinění z vměšování. V Gaze a na Západním břehu pokračují ozbrojené střety, nálety a operace navzdory příměřím. Írán mezitím hlásí sestřelení amerického dronu MQ-1 v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu, což zvyšuje napětí s USA.
archive.security_status_en: Israel is facing a deep political crisis and election deadlock after Netanyahu's bloc fell short of a majority, accompanied by foreign interference allegations. Armed clashes, raids, and military operations persist across Gaza and the West Bank despite fragile ceasefires. Meanwhile, Iran reported shooting down a US MQ-1 drone near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions with Washington.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech se očekávají intenzivní koaliční manévry a právní spory ohledně izraelských voleb, zatímco bezpečnostní složky zůstanou v ostražitosti kvůli íránské aktivitě. Diplomatický tlak na stabilizaci situace v Gaze a na Západním břehu bude nadále eskalovat.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will feature intense coalition maneuvering and legal disputes over the Israeli election, while security forces remain vigilant regarding Iranian activity. Diplomatic pressure to stabilize the situation in Gaza and the West Bank will continue to escalate.
